TextEng: A finely crafted helmet imbued with a touch of magic.

It's not certain whether the fur of these gloves is naturally green, or has been dyed, but whatever it's origin, it is most certainly supernatural and linked in some way to the Undead. While the inside of the gloves is completely safe, touching the outside with anything except extreme caution, causes an intense numbness. On occasion, strong blows with these gloves will release a charge that deals extreme damage to the recipient of the blow.
A pair of gloves, made of green fur. It's not certain whether the fur is naturally green, or has been dyed.
These robes bestow upon the wearer the ability to resist acid, as well as some minor spellcasting.

These strange stones are magic and can be rubbed along a weapon to enhance it's properties. They are particularly coveted by those with crafting skills.

<c ÿÿ>Use: Cast on yourself. The item in your right hand will receive the effect. This item does not work on ranged weapons.<cÿÿÿ>
A stone that throbs in the hand.
This badge, issued by a representative of the Crown, should be worn at all times to denote your legal status as an adventurer. However, if checked, you must also posess a valid Adventurer's Charter.

An Adventurer's Charter with the names of you and your companions on it. This Charter allows you to bear arms and adventure for one year. It used to be obligatory to make sure the names on the Charter match the individuals in a party, but in these difficult times, only the party leader's name is included.

This tattered note catches your eye:

"The Master wants you to find any secret ways into Hawklin's castle. If your mission is discovered, you are to find and silence any who know you, then return to Polter's Fort."

<c ÿÿ>Note: You should pick this note up, but do not need to keep it afterwards.<cÿÿÿ>
These simple amulets are designed for those with little regard for the law.
This animal figure can be used to increase strength on two occasions.
An archer never knows when he will find himself in a duel with someone more skilled. These bracers help even the odds.
A armlet with inscriptions around the bands.

These deceptively plain leather jerkins all came from a single tanner, who used  the blood of eagles in the tanning process. Her fame at making leather jerkins spread, boosted by a secret guild of archers who made their fortunes from winning archery competitions.

These armlets were used in the training of monks and acolytes to help them manipulate skills they would later attain for themselves. Many were stolen by those destined never to succeed as monks in their own right.
A armlet with inscriptions around the bands.

This finely crafted, light mail coat has a pale blue sheen. When the wearer presses their hand against the central ring on the chest, a dagger of ice flies forth. Over time, the mail will recharge as it takes energy from the blows that land on it.

<c ÿÿ>If you use all the charges on the item, it will crumble into dust.<cÿÿÿ>
This finely crafted, light mail coat has a pale blue sheen.
Blowing this horn will order all your troops to try and attack the enemy, committing your reserves.
A sling inscribed with webbed designs.

A bag of beans is filled with 5-20 beans. Each of these beans, if carefully removed from the bag, has a weird and wonderful power (or sometimes not so wonderful). Only five beans can be taken from the bag on any given day.

This bag of finger bones can be thrown at an enemy, whereupon it will burst open. The bones inside will magically enlarge and assemble themselves into undead skeletons, thereupon attacking their target. The skeletons are incapable of following any command, but will continue to assault the foes of their summoner.
A bag of finger bones or some such.

A bag of snuff, particularly fashionable at present with the nobility of Cormyr. Taking a sniff causes a fit of sneezing that takes a few seconds to wear off. Adventurers don't find this invention particularly useful.
A bag of wind. When opened, a strong gust of wind billows forth, knocking enemies from their feet.
A loose bag tied off with a string. If anything, it seems to be full of air.
Piecemeal or complete armors of this type offer protection that is equal to banded or splint mail. Some, like this one, have minor enchantments on them, though no maker's mark is upon them.
Bane is a black-hafted axe, set with two gold bands. Crafted for the servants of evil, this fearsome axe brings doom upon its victims.
A black-hafted axe, set with two gold bands.
These cloaks have earned the nickname 'Barbarian Cloak' because of their peculiar ability to allow the wearer to use brawn at the expense of brains.
A barrel of oil. It takes very little intelligence to work out that with a tinderbox you could set this alight...then run for it!

This map was given to you by the dragon Wyvernvapor. It should help you locate the Wyvern Crown. Unfortunately, the combination of archaic language and unrecognizable landmarks means you cannot work out which barrow holds the Crown. You will need to show this map to Lord Hawklin.

Whenever he was denied something that he desired, Beldin would grasp the buckle of this belt and intimidate his poor victim into submission. After a while, tired of his tactics, merchants began making such belts for themselves. It was not long before blades were drawn and Beldin himself was sent to the grave.
A woven belt with a brass buckle, this belt's true value lies in its ability to deaden blows.
A woven belt with a brass buckle.
This leather belt emits light when worn.

These gloves are nicknamed Bigby's gloves, because of their ability to cast the spell of that name. The likelihood is that these gloves are ancient, and may have served as a method for Bigby to test his spells in order to perfeect them. The gloves absorb the power of blows struck, eventually absorbing enough power to cast a spell. The blows must be struck with an empty hand however, and since the gloves have no other power, this means they are ownly favored by monks. Draining all the charges from the gloves will destroy them.
This leather has been darkened with a black dye.
Probably originating from Westgate, this magic leather makes the wearer a master of trickery. However, those that perceive the wearer, also find something distinctly untrustworthy about them.

These chain shirts were commonly worn by reavers in the early days of Cormyr. Dressed in their black mail shirts, the reavers silently attacked farming families, stealing not only their goods, but their women too, unless the farmers paid them off. The terms 'blackmail' and 'bereaved' soon became commonplace.
This mail shirt is made from a dark alloy of metal but otherwise is unremarkable.
This black sling is magical; a new bullet appearing within it as the last is used. It also highly accurate.
A black sling. It is not remarkable in any way except its hue.

This is a very high quality staff with a shaft of ebony, and mahogany ends tipped with solid steel.  If it strikes the head, a blow from this staff can be so hard it will stun an opponent. Blows to the hands or arms often numb the limb, causing the victim to drop their weapon.
A very high quality staff with a shaft of ebony and mahogany ends tipped with solid steel.
This magic sword was in the hands of Jonas when he arrived at the battle for the Wyvern Crown.
They say one of the ingredients in these potions is blood from a truly evil man...
These bullets are coated with some sort of anti-coagulant, leaving the victim to bleed to death.
Small stones made for a sling. They are coated in a sticky substance.

Blooddrinker literally saps the strength of the victim. If the sword drinks enough blood, it allows the wielder to temporarily increase his strength. Note that completely draining Blooddrinker will destroy it.

The blood helms belonged to a group of good-aligned paladins, who fell from grace and were twisted into evil ways. The insides of each helm are covered in rust, their peculiar vampiric powers a blasphemy for the metalwork of the helm itself.
A cylindrical basinet which is a little old, but still finely made.
These bolts have been blessed by the gods to wreak vengeance on the unworthy.
These bolts have been blessed by the gods to wreak vengeance on the undead.
Bolts that pulse in the hand.
Each bolt is marked with an ancient rune. When the bolt strikes, it seems to drain the strength of the victim.

This book is crammed full of tips, tricks, remedies and the knowledge of old antidotes. Luckily it's magical nature means that simply scanning more than a few pages transfers all the knowledge into the reader's head forever, at which point the book crumbles in to dust.

<c ÿÿ>Single use, permanent +2 Heal bonus.<cÿÿÿ>

This astonishing book is full of half-truths and deceit that sounds entirely plausible. It's magical nature means that simply scanning more than a few pages makes the reader a master of bluff forever, at which point the book crumbles in to dust.

<c ÿÿ>Single use, permanent +2 Bluff bonus.<cÿÿÿ>

This book is crammed full with assorted paraphernalia regarding artifacts, languages, lost lore, ancient history and forgotten wonders. Luckily it's magical nature means that simply scanning more than a few pages transfers all the knowledge into the reader's head forever, at which point the book crumbles in to dust.

<c ÿÿ>Single use, permanent +2 Lore bonus.<cÿÿÿ>

This book is crammed full of hints and tips on smelting and alloy-making for weaponry. Luckily it's magical nature means that simply scanning more than a few pages transfers all the knowledge into the reader's head forever, at which point the book crumbles in to dust.

<c ÿÿ>Single use, permanent +2 Craft Weapon bonus.<cÿÿÿ>
This boots were specifically made for men and women who typically travel over long distances. They are much prized by adventurers.
Simple boots. There is nothing special about them.
Woodland folk and fey creatures have been known to give these boots as gifts to those that protect the forests from wanton destruction.
Simple boots. There is nothing special about them.

This bracer is clearly dedicated to Malar, The Beastlord. Blessed by Malar, those that wear it can truly enjoy the thirst of the hunt. Followers of Malar will find the bracer has additional powers when it is worn.
These minor talismans usually have very basic magic properties.
This is a high quality breastplate with minor enchantments on it, though no maker's mark.
This golden necklace carries a holy pendant that emits a steady low light. The amulet's powers are aimed at those that must combat the Undead.
A necklace made from gold with a heavy golden pendant.
This magic breastplate is so soft that it actually absorbs blows, the bronze warping under the force, then springing back into shape.

This axe has a powerful enchantment set upon it. When it strikes an opponent, there is a 5% chance that part of the opponent's soul will be drawn into the axe, dealing catastrophic damage (+2-24) and draining 5 constitution. Each time the axe soulsucks an opponent, it uses a charge.

This daggerhas a powerful enchantment set upon it. When it strikes an opponent, there is a 5% chance that part of the opponent's soul will be drawn into the weapon, dealing catastrophic damage (+2-24) and draining 5 constitution. Each time the dagger soulsucks an opponent, it uses a charge.
A strange looking dagger with a silver tipped blade.
This rod was given to you to help you resist some of the powers of the Witch Lord.
This unspectacular-looking flail hides a fearsome magic that grants the wielder incredible speed when striking.
A light flail, unspectacular in appearance.

The Cat o' Nine Tails, or affectionately referred to as just the Cat, is a sailor's tool for dealing out punishment. The 'Lick of the Cat' is a simple way to keep discipline on board ship. This is a particularly nasty version, with steel barbs all along the tails, dipped in some kind of resin.
A black-handled whip with many tails.
A small cavalry horn typically used to rally troops. It seems this horn may have a mild enchantment upon it.
A small censer filled with a narcotic that causes drowsiness, slowness of mind or even nausea.
Made by the centaur Galuros from the hair of his comrades, these gloves make the wearer almost at one with their horse, a true centaur.
A fine coat of mail with minor enchantments on it, though no maker's mark.
A fine suit of scalemale imbued with minor enchantments, though no maker's mark.
These gauntlets are the secret behind several champions' incredible strength.
A pair of gauntlets, embroidered with a sword and hammer symbol.

The Champion's Helm is a very handsome helm with a stiffened crest, that has greater protection than a standard helm. The magic in the helm also flows through the shoulders of the wearer making their blows strong enough to knock opponents off their feet.
A very handsome helm with a stiffened crest.
Tiny sparks play over the surface of this suit of scalemail. Of unknown origin, chaos mail is made from an alloy melded with energy captured from lightning.
Scalemail with a surcoat of unknown heraldry. The mail is well made but nothing special, except that it seems slight sparks are always at the edge of sight.

The Chaos Whip is a black-handled whip with many tails. When the whip strikes, it lets off small electric shocks. The combined effect of the shock and the entrapment of some of the tails of the whip make it a dangerous weapon.
A black-handled whip with many tails.

At first look this is a simple scythe used for cutting grain, but in reality it is a magic item blessed by Chauntea. In the hands of a layman it has some powers, but those who worship Chauntea will find these powers grow in their hands.
A simple scythe used for cutting grain.
Highly crafted and expertly jointed, this plate would be the desire of any knight. When worn, the wearer becomes more noble in appearance; a leader in the eyes of the beholder.
Highly crafted and expertly jointed, this plate would be the desire of any knight.

Dragon cloaks have been specifically designed for the intrepid (or foolhardy) adventurer who seeks the dragon's hoard. By wrapping the cloak around them, the dragon hunter can protect themselves against the terrible breath weapons of these creatures.
A fine, velvet cloak embroidered with a dragon symbol.

This is a fine cloak with the sign of Cyric upon it. These cloaks are used by Cyric's evil followers to aid them as they spread lies and deception across the land. Though the cloak can be worn by anyone, followers of Cyric will find additional powers reside within the cloak when they don it.
A fine cloak with the sign of Cyric upon it.
This black cloak radiates darkness, hinting at the enchantment within it, ready to be released...
These old cloaks were made by druids for use in ancient rites that were performed in thunderstorms. The magic within the cloaks is still strong enough to be of practical use.
A fancy, collared cloak, made from wool. It has an earthy texture to it.

Dragon cloaks have been specifically designed for the intrepid (or foolhardy) adventurer who seeks the dragon's hoard. By wrapping the cloak around them, the dragon hunter can protect themselves against the terrible breath weapons of these creatures.
A fine, velvet cloak embroidered with a dragon symbol.

This is a fine cloak with the sign of Helm upon it. These cloaks are used by Helm's clerics and Paladins, offering extra protection against the forces of chaos. Though the cloak can be worn by anyone, followers of Helm will find additional powers reside within the cloak when they don it.
A fine cloak with the sign of Helm upon it.

Dragon cloaks have been specifically designed for the intrepid (or foolhardy) adventurer who seeks the dragon's hoard. By wrapping the cloak around them, the dragon hunter can protect themselves against the terrible breath weapons of these creatures.
A fine, velvet cloak embroidered with a dragon symbol.

The famous blue dragon hunter, Redgar Sigmundsson, always claimed the most important item in his armory was this cloak. This extraordinary cloak is made of some kind of shiny material that catches and reflects the light. Best used for prtection against lightning, it also offers some protection against other forces.
This extraordinary cloak is made of some kind of shiny material that catches and reflects the light.

This blue-dyed woolen cloak is dressed with feathers around the top that have been taken from an owl. The cloak itself imbues upon the wearer some of the advantages of an owl, though if all the feathers should come loose, the cloak loses its powers.
A blue-dyed woolen cloak, dressed with feathers around the top.

This is a fine cloak with the sign of Torm upon it. These cloaks are used by Torm's clerics and paladins, offering extra protection against the forces of evil. Though the cloak can be worn by anyone, followers of Torm will find additional powers reside within the cloak when they don it.
A fine cloak with the sign of Torm upon it.

Since the war with the Devil Dragon, these blades are fairly common in Cormyr. They were manufactured in large numbers to equip the Purple Dragons, for it was only with Cold Iron that the ghazneths could be harmed.

Since the war with the Devil Dragon, these blades are fairly common in Cormyr. They were manufactured in large numbers to equip the Purple Dragons, for it was only with Cold Iron that the ghazneths could be harmed.

Many of these weapons can be found across Cormyr and the surrounding lands, They were forged during the war with the Devil Dragon and carried by many Purple Dragon and noble alike. Only a cold iron blade could wound a ghazneth.
These minor talismans usually have very basic magic properties.
A shield bearing the Cormaeril Coat of Arms.
A finely crafted dagger with a hardened alloy blade.

These cylindrical helms were one of several items made for some of the important nobles of Cormyr when King Azoun IV set out on the Crusade against the Tuigan Horde. Against foes in numbers, courage can easily falter.
A cylindrical basinet which is a little old, but still finely made.

This crystal ball is an ancient magic device that detects the fog on Lake Wyvernwater. The Keeper told you that removing the ball from its resting place will break the link with the Mythallar and the castle would sink back into the lake. 

<c ÿÿ>Destroying the ball will break the link permanently. Use the ball if you wish to do so.<cÿÿÿ>
The swiftest dancers sometimes used magical aid. These boots make the wearer light-footed and nimble beyond the ordinary.
Simple boots. There is nothing special about them.

Though large, this odd, spear-like weapon is extremely lightweight, crafted from strange alloys. In hand it almost has a life of its own. Any warrior who grasps this weapon finds themselves incredibly fast in combat, capable of astonishing spins and whirls.
Though large, this odd, spear-like weapon is extremely lightweight, crafted from strange alloys.
These arrows will drive even the brave away.

You can target this at a henchman to kill it.     You can target it on a dead henchman to ressurrect them.

This is intended for testing problems with mounted henchmen deaths.
In the depths of the woods, the most skillfull of rangers ply their skills. Deepwood leather offers the protection of heavier mail suits, while leaving the wearer free to move.
This shield, although plain in appearance, hides a strong enchantment that casts a protective field around the bearer.
With a last minute twist, any blow can be partially avoided. This is the secret power of Deft Boots.
Simple boots. There is nothing special about them.
This holy dagger is blessed by Deneir with wards of protection. In the hands of those that worship Deneir its powers grow.
An ornate dagger engraved with the symbol of Deneir.

This small dart is made of pewter, ivory, and fine fletching from some exotic bird.  It doesn't appear to be very useful in combat, but is perfectly balanced for some kind of game.  There is also a slight vibration to it.

This item can be targetted at a horse, placeable, door, etc. to get additional information which you can include in your mantis bug reports.   This will hopefully help us narrow down certain types of problems faster than in the past.
Beta Testers Object Debug Data Dump
Well crafted and balanced swords, these weapons only come into their own against the mightiest of foe.
A finely wrought, two-handed sword, with a winged guard.

Drelb, a famed assassin in the Night Masks, had two blades, both originally stolen from temples of different religions, one dedicated to Malar, the other to Chauntea. This longer blade is dedicated to Chauntea, and her worshippers will be able to unlock the additional powers of the blade.
A very fine rapier, set with a small inexpensive gemstone.

Drelb, a famed assassin in the Night Masks, had two blades, both originally stolen from temples of different religions, one dedicated to Malar, the other to Chauntea. This short blade is dedicated to Malar, and his worshippers will be able to unlock the additional powers of the blade.
This scimitar has an ornate guard and a hilt wrapped with shagreen dyed black. When frimly gripped, a great calm settles on the wielder allowing superior clarity of thought in battle.
A scimitar with an ornate guard. The hilt is wrapped with shagreen dyed black.
When teaching, it can be necessary to be proficient with every weapon..
Chainmail armor like this is most likely a relic left over from the elves of Cormanthyr. It is lightweight and masterfully crafted, with colours that blend with the forest on a summer morning.
A suit of chainmail made from a light, flexible steel. To the untrained eye it looks special.
Chainmail shirts like this one are most likely a relic left over from the elves of Cormanthyr. It is lightweight and masterfully crafted, with colors that blend with the forest on a summer morning.
A fine chain shirt made from a lightweight metal of some sort.
Cormyr lies now in the realm of what was once the elvish realm of Cormanthyr, and some elvish items can still be found. This is one of the most common and most useful of them.
An attractive and slightly ornamental woodsman's cloak.

An empty bottle with a stopper.

<c ÿÿ>Note: Bottles are filled by placing them in a container which has a liquid in it. If drunk from they are consumed.<cÿÿÿ>

An enchanting stone can be rubbed on a weapon to temporarily enhance it. The more skillful the crafter, the better the enhancement, which typically lasts about 4 minutes. Truly great weaponsmiths can sometimes make the enhancement stick permanently, although no smith has managed to get one of these stones to work on a weapon that already has an enhancement bonus on it.

<c ÿÿ>Use: Cast on the melee weapon of your choice. Note: Do not use the Enchanting Stone on a weapon that already has a +1 (or more) bonus to hit/damage, nor on a ranged weapon.<cÿÿÿ>
A much enhanced version of the ring of protection, probably made by a minor Artificer.
Unspectacular in appearance, but special nevertheless, this crossbow requires no ammunition of its own.
The head of your father. In death his face is calm and noble. With no tools to bury his body, and scavengers about, perhaps you can at least find somewhere to bury his head.
A very basic wand, that is used to frighten enemies.
Brewed by goblins and hobgoblins, this potion is used to bolster prowess in battle.
A thick, black liquid obtained from a pot.
Finely crafted chainmail that weighs much less than it would appear.
Finely crafted Plate Mail, with reduced weight.

This beautiful, collared cape is made of some soft material, and dyed with vibrant colors.  The lining feels warm to the touch, belying the hidden powers withing the cape. Five times, the wearer can call forth flames to lash their enemies, then the cloak becomes useless.
A beautiful, collared cape made of some soft material, and dyed with vibrant colors. The lining of the cape feels warm to the touch.

The Fire Knives are a group of exiled nobles of Cormyr who seek to destabilize the country through murders. One theory is that they took their name from these weapons - easy to conceal, yet lethal to their foes.
A fine jerkin of leather darkened and ensorcelled for use by senior members of the Fire Knives. This group of assassins are sworn to the destruction of the nobility of Cormyr.
A fine jerkin of leather, darkened and possibly ensorcelled in some way.
These robes bestow upon the wearer the ability to resist fire, as well as some minor spellcasting.

These strange stones are magic and can be rubbed along a weapon to enhance it's properties. They are particularly coveted by those with crafting skills.

<c ÿÿ>Use: Cast on yourself. The item in your right hand will receive the effect. This item does not work on ranged weapons.<cÿÿÿ>
A stone that throbs in the hand.
These arrows have a minor enchantment on them, that makes them burst into flame in flight.

Dedicated to Tempus, the Foeslayer is a battleaxe for war, pure and simple. It's fine balance will benefit any wielder, although those that follow Tempus will find it a more powerful weapon, releasing its hidden powers once the axe is in their hands.
A solid and simple battleaxe. There is no mark upon this weapon.

This odd-looking ring is made of some kind of green wood and carved with leaves around the band. As well as slowly healing the wearer, this ring seems to call upon the power of Silvanus to grant other powers. Followers of Silvanus will find the ring has additional hidden benefits.
This odd-looking ring is made of some kind of green wood and carved with leaves around the band.
Brewed by goblins and hobgoblins, this potion is used to bolster prowess in battle.
A murky brew obtained from a pot.
A fine sword with vague rivulets of blue running through the blade. Originally this blade was a fine weapon, but at some point it has been cursed, although some of the original enchantment survives.
A fine sword with vague rivulets of blue running through the blade.
This beautifully crafted suit of full plate bears no maker's mark, but carries a minor enchantment.
For a while, these odd seeds became high fashion at balls and social gatherings. They bestow an odd, ghostly effect on those that eat them.
A collection of seeds with an oily coating.
These belts are found in all walks of life where fire is a common hazard.
Simple in appearance, these belts give the wearer a boost to their strength.
These simple belts would pass unnoticed if not for the giant buckle. Of unknown origin, they hold within them hidden clerical powers.
A belt of leather with a large buckle.
Once touched, these gloves magically graft themselves onto the skin. The curse they carry makes the wearer fumble things in their hands.
This pair of gloves clearly belongs to an Order of Fighting Monks, though its specific origins are lost.
The heart of a shattered Gem Golem, a flawless ruby.
The heart of a shattered Gem Golem, a flawless emerald.
The heart of a shattered Gem Golem, a flawless diamond.
The heart of a shattered Gem Golem, a flawless jewel.
Given to you by Caladnei, this mace will help you should you encounter any of the Gem Golems reputed to guard the barrow of the Wyvern Crown.
A simple band of gold, with a single semi-precious stone held in place, solitaire style. This is a superior version of a Ring of Protection.
A simple band of gold, with a single semi-precious stone held in place, solitaire style.

These helmets have a thin, transparent material across the eyeslits, that help the wearer see. The aid is magical in nature though, and it takes a while to get used to the strange vision granted. The Greater version of the Truesight helm allows the user to see through illusions so well, that often they can avoid them entirely.
These wands give light upon a magic command. Unfortunately it takes a smattering of Power to be able to use them, and although available to most, they are not available to all.

This small shield is made of beech wood, and reinforced with hazel. Blessed by Silvanus, its strengths lie in combatting the unnatural. Worshippers of Silvanus will find the growth of the forest in their veins.
A small shield made of beech wood, and reinforced with hazel.

These fine bows are so called because the tension in their strings makes them resonate like a harp when they are used.This is no coincidence, since they were made for a strange order of warrior bards many years ago. Not just highly functional weapons, they also amplify the powers of bardic users, though the slight hum the bow makes can be a nuisance.
A very fine composite longbow, ready strung.
A suit of chainmail with the Hawklin coat of arms.
A suit of plate with the Hawklin coat of arms.
A suit of platel with the Hawklin coat of arms.
A shield bearing the Hawklin Coat of Arms.
This ornate helm is made from a combination of metal and what look like  dragon scales. Though the scales are immitations, the helm does have some of the powers of a dragon.
An ornate helm made from a combination of metal and what look like scales.
This ornate helm is made from a combination of metal and what look like  dragon scales. Though the scales are immitations, the helm does have some of the powers of a dragon.
An ornate helm made from a combination of metal and what look like scales.
This ornate helm is made from a combination of metal and what look like  dragon scales. Though the scales are immitations, the helm does have some of the powers of a dragon.
An ornate helm made from a combination of metal and what look like scales.
There is no knowing who designed or made these ancient helms, but they have proved useful through the ages.
These odd helmets allow the wearer to breath underwater.
This strange helmet is one of several made by the folk that dwell beneath the Lake of Dragons on Cormyr's southern shore.
A suit of scalemail belonging to the Purple Dragons.
Probably crafted by a tribal smith, this barbaric looking hide armor has a minor enchantment on it.
These wood and horn bows are specially designed for use on horseback. With the magic within them, riding and shooting becomes easy.

Hultail Spirits are famous for their potency. The imbiber becomes almost instantly inebriated for a short period of time, but with the drunkenness also come feelings of intense strength and invincibility.

Effects that last for 2 minutes:
Drunk -1 to hit
Strength +1
Will Saves +2.

Effects that last for 2 and a half minutes:
-3 to spot skill.
A suit of chainmail with the Huntcrown coat of arms.
A shield bearing the Huntcrown Coat of Arms.

This document is a solemn oath sworn by Lord Marvin Huntcrown not to hunt the Forest Folk of Hullack Forest. This document would be ample proof for Manthis the satyr that you have stopped the hunting of his kin.
These fine bows certainly make the job of hunting a much easier task.

The greatest Masters of the Hunt were not only those that handled their animals best, but also got amongst their pack. When the hunters closed for the kill, the Huntmaster needed protection from the stray arrows of the novice.
A plain, woolen cloak with a dyed edge.
A suit of chainmail with the Huntsilver coat of arms.
A shield bearing the Huntsilver Coat of Arms.
This copper necklace holds a strange jewel in it that catches the light in weird angles. The jewel hints at the powers that lie within the amulet; powers of hypnotism and bewilderment.
This copper necklace holds a strange jewel in it that catches the light in weird angles.
These robes bestow upon the wearer the ability to resist cold, as well as some minor spellcasting.

These strange stones are magic and can be rubbed along a weapon to enhance it's properties. They are particularly coveted by those with crafting skills.

<c ÿÿ>Use: Cast on yourself. The item in your right hand will receive the effect. This item does not work on ranged weapons.<cÿÿÿ>
A stone that throbs in the hand.

A quick scan of this note reveals it to be from the merchant Imelda, Lord Hawklin's business partner:

Valetto will pay dearly for all of the goods he has stolen from me with his piracy, and for the deaths of my crewmen. I don't care who you work for or how you do it, but I want Valetto to suffer as I have suffered. I am prepared to pay 500 golden lions for every farm of Valetto's that is destroyed."
This heavy cloak has magically been formed from a sheet of iron. Though a cloak, it offers significant protection. However fire and cold based attacks are conducted easily through the cloak.
These minor talismans usually have very basic magic properties.
A small piece of ivory. Ivory is an important commodity in Cormyr, and even a small piece is worth something.
A beautiful ring with some cut gems on it. It should fetch a few gold!
A simple charm on a length of rawhide that might be worth a few coppers. You remember that Jonas once had a charm like this one.
This odd kama has strange rainbow-like patterns in the metal. When swung, these colours catch the light, and when tinted with fresh blood can hypnotise the unfortunate victim - just like a cobra.
A strange Eastern weapon with a many-hued head,
A reinforced leather jerkin with a dark leather cloak, finely made.

These simple looking weapons are magically enchanted, causing confusion in those unfortunate enough to be struck squarely by them.

Dedicated to Silvanus, these spears bring blight and putrification on any wound inflicted. If wielded by a follower of Silvanus, the powers within the spear grow.
This odd-shaped spear has a blade that appears to be darkened to almost black with rust, but closer inspection reveals it is made of some strange material.

No different from a normal longbow, except this one has been made from Yew by a master Bowyer. The pull of the bow is signifcantly greater than a standard longbow. This will not benefit weaker characters (less than strength 12 cannot even use it), but stronger characters will be able to use the extra pull. The bow is not magic however, so only costs a few gold more than an average longbow.

On equiping, the bow will grant a Mighty bonus dependant on strength:
minimum for a +1 bonus = 14
minimum for a +2 bonus = 17

Mail of Fleetness is a suit of chainmail, with a tabbard showing the head of a stag. The quality of the steel links is very fine, reflecting woodland hues under full light. The lightness of the make, and the magic cast cunningly in the joints, both aid the wearer's speed.
A beautiful suit of chainmail, with a tabbard showing the head of a stag. The quality of the steel links is very fine, reflecting woodland hues under full light.

A suit of mail and plate. In the centre is  what looks like a hole into...nothing. Sliced from a Sphere of Anihilation, the hole swallows many blows that land on the mail. Once a day, darkness can be made to spew forth from the hole.
A suit of mail and plate. In the centre is  what looks like a hole into...nothing.

Named for the surcoat that is an integral part of this magic suit, Mail of the Eagle grants the wearer piercing sight. In addition, the mail absorbs the power of blows. Once enough power has been absorbed it can be released as a burst of energy by the wearer, increasing their speed.

<c ÿÿ>If you use all the charges on the item, it will crumble into dust.<cÿÿÿ>
A suit of full mail with lighter protection for the shield arm.
This chainmail has been imbued with magical properties that increase the wearer's defenses, particularly against negative forces.
Chain mail with a slight blue tint to it.

When the finest knights of Cormyr were enchanted and laid to rest against a future time of emergency, they were each equipped with a suit of mail that was almost peerless in quality. The knights themselves were slain or corrupted by the ghazneths during the war, so very few of these suits survived the appetite of the ghazneths.
Very fine but obviously old chainmail.
Melf's rods are made by magicians to hold repertoires of acid spells.
This Merchant's Charter allows you to carry arms for the period of seven days without Peacestrings, so that you can legally be employed to defend a caravan.
These rings are worn by many a merchant. They have value from the semi-precious stones they hold, but are also wrought with more subtle virtues.

Delivered by messenger bird, this lays out Sir Gilbert Hawklin's reply to your message regarding the source of the raiders. It orders you to join 'Edgar Truesilver' who is hunting raiders targeting a barrow near Four Oaks Farm. However you are not sure where this barrow is. Perhaps Manthis can help you?

This messenger bird was given to you by Sir Gilbert Hawklin. He has told you to release it with information on the origin of the raids, should you uncover the truth.

<c ÿÿ>Note: To release the bird, 'use' it. It is assumed that when you do so you have written and attached the appropriate message. <cÿÿÿ>

This fine rapier, set with a small inexpensive gemstone, is dedicated to Milil, Lord of Song. It's beauty benefits the wearer, but only a follower of Milil will see the true benefits of this weapon. Once in hand, its hidden powers will be revealed to them.
A very fine rapier, set with a small inexpensive gemstone.

These strange amulets are used by members of the Night Masks, a shady organisation of thieves and other undesirables  in their work in Westgate. A moment of deep concentration allows the wearer to become more perceptive - without the need to keep concentrating - useful when the bearer needs the mind clear for other things.

A succesful concentration check will grant a bonus equal to the wearer's concentration skill to the following skills for a period of 5 minutes:
spot
search
listen
A large stone held on a brass chain. The stone swirls with misty colours.
A suit of leather armor, worked with weird sigils. Almost certainly the work of a mad artificer, this strange armor imbues fear in those who touch it, including the wearer.
A suit of leather armor, worked with weird sigils.

Moonbane is made from a white metal and dedicated to the goddess Selune. Clouds seem to move across its surface, a suggestion of the powerful enchantments within - enchantments that are greater in the hands of a follower of Selune.
A mace made from a white metal. Clouds seem to move across its surface, as if it hides from the sun.

Morphion's Covetous Ring seems like a handy item that increases the user's ability to bargain and deal with money matters. Unfortunately, it is also cursed; the avarice in the face of the wearer cannot be hidden.
A beautiful ring, of certain value.
When thrown, this lethal dust spreads into a deadly enchanted cloud.

They say the enchantments upon these helms are only possible with the blood of virgins slain at midnight on a New Moon, although this may be doubtful considering just how many of these helms can be found.
A bottle of highly explosive blended naptha, an ingredient used often for siege weaponry. It has other uses, the simplest of which is to throw it.
Necromulets are special amulets that focus the powers of Necromancers.
Nightblade is the name of a group of swords used by the Night Masks of Westgate for their assassinations. Even a slight wound is often enough to bring the victim down.
A fine jerkin of leather darkened and ensorcelled for use by senior members of the Night Masks. The wearer becomes incredibly nimble and stealthy.
A fine jerkin of leather darkened and possibly ensorcelled in some way.
These odd potions were probably made by drow and used when venturing onto the surface.

Though highly ornamental in appearance, this suit of plate is still functional and carries a very minor magic upon it. Probably it belonged to some knightly Order, though the Coat-of-Arms is unfamiliar.
This suit of plate seems highly ornamental, and probably belongs to some knightly Order.
These fine clothes are thick enough to constitute some protection, and also carry a minor enchantment.
These gloves are attuned to the benefit of only the purest of spirits.
A pair of gloves made of an expensive-looking, pale blue leather.
Use this item to eliminate a horse that you cannot get rid of.
A helmet usually worn by heavily armored soldiers of the Purple Dragons.

A set of armor with the unmistakable colors of the Purple Dragons.

A shield from a soldier of Cormyr, a Purple Dragon.

This item is considered stolen if you take it.
Clearly the armlets of some skilled bard, and some of that skill has become embedded in the armlets.
A armlet with inscriptions around the bands.

It is not known who first crafted Pinpoint arrows, but is almost certain they were an attempt to aid in combat in the dark places. With this solution, a champion could at least find and finish any foe he had hit with an arrow.
This sling was wielded by a notorious highway robber. Somewhere along the line, this semi-sentient sling began to absorb some of the cruelty of its owner.
A sling embroidered with dark markings.
Not quite up to the same protection of full plate, this plate mail is nevertheless very well crafted and has additional encantations cast upon it.

This is a large denomination Platinum Trade Bar. Trade Bars are often used in Cormyr and other countries by merchants who are not carrying Cormyrean currency. Platinum Trade Bars are particularly rare.
A pair of green gloves that make even the most uneducated an expert in the use, and avoidance, of poisons.
A pair of green gloves without any obvious properties.

The restless spirit of a poltergeist resides within this blade. Already bested by you, the spirit is now bound by your command. Twice per day its power can be released to flow through you, increasing your strength and dexterity 5 each for a period of a few minutes.
This thick, bright orange potion is of unknown origin, but grants the drinker the ability to change shape.

The old swamp witch Maya had an uncanny ability to catch those that tried to steal any of her hidden treasures, so much so that everyone believed she had eyes in the back of her head. The truth really lay in her continuous drinking of these potions which she made herself, preferring them to a glass of wine.
These are the battle potions of an Order of Tempus, commonly brewed for use by warriors before combat.
A potion of protection vs magic.
With skin as hard as stone, there is little that can stop you...
These powerfull potions strengthen the will of the drinker, making them highly resistant to mind-affecting spells and effects.

A heavy hammer made from what looks like cast iron crudely attached to a shaft. It's shoddy craftsmanship, or is it just a show?

This brass ring has several sharp projections on it. The careless could easily cut themselves.

This amulet carries a small, enamel face. It is not ordinary amulet; the face can see and hear, warning the wearer of hidden dangers with whispered words.
Carved with an enamel face, this amulet is clearly magical, although you have no idea of its powers.

Your father always kept these pieces of his sword safe after the war. The blade itself was broken by the same stroke of the Devil Dragon's tail that wrecked your father's arm. Your father always claimed the weapon was magical, and intended to one day reforge it.
All that is left of the fine sword that was once posessed by the poltergeist of Polter's Fort. After you sprinkled it with Holy Water, the weapon was destroyed, leaving only a few fragments.

Clearly this magical spearhead was once attached to a haft, but whatever became of it is not known to you. Though this spearhead must have lain in the barrow where you found it for ages, it remains untouched by time, and gleams coolly with its own light.

It is not clear whether this was the blade of a polearm or axe, but what is clear is that it is magical, emitting a very faint hum. To be of any use it would need to be reforged, though whether it would retain any magic is another question.

This shield is enscribed with an old Cormyrian heraldric symbol, as evidenced by the Purple Dragon. The device isn't just symbolic though: from the dragon stems the power to breath dragon breath once per day, and from the towers, the strength to resist blows.
A shield enscribed with an old Cormyrian heraldric symbol.
This wand can fire highly charged balls of energy.
These robes bestow upon the wearer the ability to resist shock, either electrical or sound, as well as some minor spellcasting.

These strange stones are magic and can be rubbed along a weapon to enhance it's properties. They are particularly coveted by those with crafting skills.

A stone that throbs in the hand.

A specially prepared vial of Holy Water that is supposed to be used to exorcise poltergeists. It can only be used by sprinkling it on the poltergeist. The difficult part is subduing the poltergeist first.

This leather armor is made from the tanned hides of unknown animals and dedicated to Silvanus. It bestows the resistance of a great Oak upon the wearer, and if that wearer worships Silvanus, the powers grow further when the armor is donned.
Leather armour made from the tanned hides of unknown animals.
Silver tipped arrows. Expensive, but useful against werebeasts.
Silver tipped arrows. Expensive, but useful against werebeasts.
This is a small, silver chalice with a leaf motif. Of unknown origin, it fills with a clear liquid each day. When drunk, this liquid has minor healing powers.
A small, silver chalice with a leaf motif.
A finely crafted dagger with a hardened alloy blade made with silver and cold iron.
A strange looking dagger with a silver tipped blade.
This mirror does not reflect, but instead shows a perfect silver sheen.
This is a large denomination Silver Trade Bar. Trade Bars are often used in Cormyr and other countries by merchants who are not carrying Cormyrean currency.

Relics of an ancient time, these stones can be used to place virtues on an item. The results can be unpredictable, even detrimental at times, although are more reliable in the hands of those that can craft.

<c ÿÿ>Use: Cast on the item you wish to receive the effect.<cÿÿÿ>
A stone that throbs in the hand.

Slicer is very fine sickle with a golden blade and an ebony handle. The blade itself is not gold, but made from some magical alloy that carries a very keen edge - so keen that it is reputed to cause wounds that go beyond the Material Plane, so that preventing the bleeding caused by this weapon is incredibly difficult.
A very fine sickle with a golden blade and an ebony handle.

This thin spear has an incredibly sharp tip, and the shaft appears to be made from ebony. The magic that resides in the weapon allows the spear to cut through armour like butter, letting the cold freeze the victim's veins.
A thin spear with an incredibly sharp tip. The shaft appears to be made from ebony.

A pair of gloves such as these were reputedly used once by a great smith, who had enhanced them to use in a smithing competition. He had hoped that by enchanting a pair of plain gloves he would escape detection from the judges. Whether he succeeded or not is not recorded, but the idea was soon copied.
A pair of brown leather gloves.
Made from the skin of a specific species of snake, this cloak is easily adapted for magic. Often the magic takes the form of the snakes it comes from.
A long cloak made from the skin of some reptile.

This staff is made of a dark wood, then bound with iron, and topped with heavy lead ends. Within resides an ancient magic, binding a cobra to the staff. When the staff strikes its opponent, the cobra's head shoots from the tip and attempts to bite. Once per day, the cobra can be released from the staff, though it is not intelligent and will only attack foes that it sees.
A staff made of a dark wood, then bound with iron, and topped with heavy lead ends.
A pair of very fine leather boots. They are not magical, but they are excellent workmanship.

A heavy, velvet cloak with ermine speckles sewn across it.
These protective amulets are often commissioned by those of wealth to protect themselves from the deprivations of unscrupulous wizards.
This amulet is clearly magical, although you have no idea of its powers.
This Figurine of Wonderous Power can be used to summon a giant spider 3 times.

These deceptively plain shields offer no additional protection to the bearer, unless a special command word is spoken, whereupon lights dance around the bearer. For a short duration of a few minutes, the defenses of the bearer are greatly enhanced, especially against spells and mind based attacks.
A plain wooden shield with a large metal boss in the center.
Piecemeal or complete armors of this type offer protection that is equal to banded or splint mail. This one has an enchantment on it, though no maker's mark.

This simple silver band is set with two garnets, but its true value lies in the protective spells upon it. Designed for commanders before battle, its powers will benefit anyone whose courage is in danger of wavering.
This simple silver band is set with two garnets, and should fetch a good price at market.
Starfire generates a static charge when striking something. Eventually the charge builds up so much it can be released in a burst of energy. Note that completely draining Starfire will destroy it.
Even passing close to this weapon makes the hairs stand up on your skin.

So named because of the stud-like buttons on the hilt, this sword is an unusual magic weapon. Slightly magical in its own right, the sword's buttons have additional powers. It's not certain whether the sword is part mechanical or purely magic driven.
This sword has a number of button-like studs on the hilt. Surely it's magical?
This studded leather jerkin has a very mild magic in it, though no maker's mark.

A simple band of gold, with a single precious stone held in place solitaire style.

Jousting is an ancient tradition in Cormyr and many other lands. In times of peace, it has always been difficult for aspiring knights and lords to find a way to prove their prowess to their peers or their king. Jousting became a method for one knight to prove his superiority over another. Soon such contests became more formal, and even the right to hold a tournament itself became a source of influence. Jousting is now a very popular way to gain fame, influence or even power. 

The aim in a joust is to unseat your opponent from his or her horse, by means of a specially designed jousting lance. These lances are specially designed to break on impact in order to lessen the chance of injuries, but a perfect blow is still more likely to unseat an opponent than leave them in the saddle.

Arcane language has sprung up around jousting, and it is now commonplace to refer to strikes by the area of the shield they aim for:

Pale: the central line running vertically down the shield
Fess: The central line running horizontally across the shield
Chief: The top third of the shield
Base: The bottom third of the shield
Sinister: The left side of the shield
Dexter: The right side of the shield

Scoring
Jousting matches are split into bouts, or 'tilts'. In each bout the two opponents ride at each other. The scoring for a bout is as follows:

Opponent unseated - 3 points
Opponent's helm struck - 2 points
Competitor's own lance breaks - 1 point

When either competitor has reached 3 points, they have won the match. In the case of a tie, the bouts continue until one or other jouster has more points. Typically points are denoted using flags. Most tournament masters use only three flags for each competitor. A fourth flag is only used to denote a winner in the case of a tie-break situation.

Aggressive Strikes
The aggressive strikes in jousting are considered to be Pale Chief, Pale Fess and Helm. Typically these blows are more likely to score points, though the downside of using these strikes is that they limit the knight's seating, in turn making them more vulnerable.

Defensive Strikes
All other strikes are considered defensive. They are still capable of yielding points, and they have an added advantage that the knight who uses them can also change his posture more freely.

Posture
There are several postures a knight can use when jousting. Some blows require careful aiming, and as such the knight cannot lean to one side or the other, nor lower his head. More defensive strikes make it easier to lean to one side, or to duck the head and reduce the target area. Sinister Fess is the only strike that gives total freedom of posture.

Glancing Blows
Not all blows score points, but even so jousting is a difficult and tough sport, and even a glancing blow may unsettle an opponent. Knights that are struck in such a way often become shaken and unable to adjust their posture properly. Those that are struck by a second such blow become stunned and are unable to adjust their posture at all. Even a further glancing blow will unseat a knight in such a situation.

Infamy & Injury
Jousting is a noble sport, conducted by knights. Though the sport is dangerous, it is not considered acceptable behaviour to attempt to injure your opponent; injuries are common enough. Even so, there are those that do use any means to win tourneys, and it is well known for example that Pale Chief is a strike that is more likely to injure the opponent. Knights that consistently injure their opponents soon gain an unchivalrous reputation. Most tournaments now have clerics on hand to heal injuries, so that such tactics do not benefit unscrupulous knights. It is said that the jeers of the crowd have unsettled some unscrupulous  knights, making them more susceptible to glancing blows.

The founding of the Kingdom of Cormyr and the identity of the first King in Suzail is debated among scholars.  One minor school of thought considers a farmer known only as  "Mondar" the first leader of the settlement of Suzail, and, accordingly, the true "first king". 

A more popular theory among historians in the Royal Court holds that Ondeth Obarskyr was, in fact, the first king of Cormyr.  There is no dispute that Ondeth Obarskyr was, in his day, the true leader of his people; however, Ondeth did not style himself as a king. Indeed, Ondeth refused the title of king and any crown that was purported to be granted or affirmed by the elves. Ondeth is famed among his descendants for supposedly vowing loudly "no title is preferable to one tainted by a false duty of fealty to any elven sovereign". 

Whatever the case, the court historians generally agree that about 1,350 years ago in The Year of Opening Doors (26 DR)  Faerlthann Obarskyr, son of Ondeth met with the elven King Iliphar Nelnueve, Lord of the Scepters and his court near the ruined site of a famous goblin raid.  There, Iliphar gave to Faerlthann Obarskyr the circlet of Cormanthor from his own brow and the first knights of Cormyr knelt to swear fealty to House Obarskyr.
House Obarskyr - The Royal Lineage of Cormyr

Legends tell of a White Stag that roams eastern Cormyr. This legend is a persistent one. It's older than the lifespan of a normal deer, so it is likely that if the White Stag exists, it is either magic, or a rare mutation of a more common species that occurs more regularly. The legend of the Stag's existence is strongest in Thunderstone, and from time to time there have been local competitions to hunt the Stag in Hullack Forest. A look at the sightings of the Stag point to a more likely place to find it being the shores of Lake Wyvernwater. No one has ever been up close to the Stag - it is reputed to be as swift as the wind, and since no hunter will ever risk a shot for fear of damaging it's hide, the White Stag lives on.

From each of the Eight great Schools of Magic, the Thayans choose from among their order the greatest to act as Councillor. The progression of the Thayans, and the growing threat this sinister force from the East poses, is very much a consequence of those chosen to sit on their High Council over the years.

In their harsh tongue, the Councillor is a "Zulkir", an Arch Wizard. Their names and identities change over the centuries - but one does not change; the Necromancer endures and does not die. Mothers and Old Wives' whisper the name "zulkir" to frighten children to stay in bed and eat their suppers. In the East, the name of the Zulkir of Necromancy turns the bowels of even hardened soldiers to water: Szass Tam.

This is a collection of notes, tattered remains of scrolls and a few faded wax rubbings, loosely collected under a pair of green copper cover plates. The patina has discoloured some of the contents. The papers seem random and unconnected, although many are in the ancient tongue of the Netherese.  A cursory reading of the papers reveals the reappearance of one name throughout: Ioulaum.

On one parchment in bold script is the following: "The secret to the mythallar is apparent, though the means of its manufacture is wholly lost. Despite all efforts, the path to the knowledge is blocked. The gods themselves seem to be actively thwarting its rediscovery. But that which was once known cannot be unknown for all time.  Ioulaum discovered the secret, somewhere relatively early in his life's journey.  It follows that by tracing the paths of his life, one might gain the key insight to its rediscovery."

A scholarly treatise on the undead.  The ancient manuscript is brittle and rarely illuminating.  One passage is marked and catches the reader's eye:

"It should be observed then that the manner of becoming undead is various: it may be bestowed as a curse by the gods; self-imposed by the spirit that will not depart from its  body such as with a ghost; inflicted upon the flesh by another of the undead, like the  ghoul or vampire, or the undead might be created by some priest or necromancer as a servant.  There are other means as well.

But for all the myriad of manners, gestations and creations of these undead, the lich stands apart, unique. Lichdom is the result of individual choice; never chance.  Lichdom cannot be forced upon anyone. Of such terrible power so as to defy even death itself, those few who achieve lichdom do so obsessed with their own self and a contempt for the natural order of life. A lich does not choose undeath over death; rather, it chooses unlife as its personal answer to oblivion.

It is fortunate that the sheer drive and singleness of purpose necessary to achieve lichdom necessarily precludes much more than a passing interest in the world itself. More fortunate still that the ego and sheer willpower of the lich prevents it from long serving or dealing with those few others of its kind. What hope for the world would there be if such paragons of arcane power could be persuaded to devote their unlives to the same cause - or choose to serve the same master?"

This book by an anonymous author chronicles the role of subterfuge and assassination in the politics of Cormyr over the centuries. In particular, one secret organization of spies and assassins has continuously resurfaced and reappeared in Cormyrean politics - the fabled "Fire Knives".

The central tenet of the book details the author's theory that the legend of the Fire Knives is wholly false and deceptive.  

The original Fire Knives began well over four centuries ago, in the wake of Cormyr's destruction of the army of the Witch Lords in 900DR.  The book theorizes that the Fire Knives arose from the ashes of the routed army of the Witch Lords and was secretly lead by some of its human lieutenants who evaded capture.  The author believes that this original group of assassins murdered, poisoned and strangled many members of the Cormyrean nobility in revenge attacks throughout the 10th century before ultimately being rooted out and destroyed by the War Wizards.  

The author details how the presence of "the Fire Knives" skips generations in the centuries since their initial appearance, suggesting not a waxing and waning of one organization, but of the creation of many individual organizations over a course of years.  The Fire Knives is thus not one organization, but many groups who each simply chose for their identity "the Fire Knives" in order to add prestige and mystery to a new gang with a new agenda.   

Whatever the case, a recent entry in a different hand in pages tucked into the back of the book confirms that the last incarnation of the Fire Knives was shattered four years ago in 1369DR. Stripped of their lands, the remains of the noble Houses of Bleth and Cormaeril were exposed as the current organizers of the Fire Knives. The remnants of those two noble houses hastily fled Cormyr. The whereabouts of the Bleths and Cormaerils are unknown, but in the margin, the word "Westgate" is underlined, followed by three large question marks.

The Kingdom of Cormyr, sometimes known as the Wolf Woods, has transformed over the centuries as the abode of dragons, elves and now, humans.

While the elven influence is greatly diminished in present day Cormyr, the remains of the ancient elven kingdom of Cormanthor glitters here and there in its twilight, with ruins and legacies of elder days buried in dark vales and hidden amidst deep moss. 

Nowhere else in Cormyr is this more evident than the Hullack Forest. Once forming the eastern border of Cormyr, the depths of the forest contain not only the secrets of the old elves and their abandoned ruins, but aberrations and other strange ghostly creatures. The forest is wild and often dark. 

Scholars say that the wild creatures of the Hullack are descendants of creatures that the elves once used to stock the edges of the forest of old Cormanthor to dissuade human expansion. In those days the forest was far larger and extended south to the edges of the Vast Swamp.

Despite the efforts of a recent expansion program encouraged by the late King Azoun IV and the heavy labours of many brave settlers and loggers, the Hullack Forest defies pacification and resists attempts to cut it back. The ancient magic of the old growth forest runs deep and its secrets are not easily explored or tamed. Still, little by little, the forest has receded over the centuries and is now but a shadow of its former glory.

Just as important as House Obarskyr in the formation of the Royal Court of Cormyr is the position of Royal Magician. 

Unlike that role in many other kingdoms in the Realms, the responsibilities of the Royal Magicians of Cormyr have always been firmly grounded not merely in magical authority but as prime minister to the Crown.  The Royal Magicians' role as politicians and first ministers flowed out of their historical duties as ambassadors to the elven court.

The first of the Royal Magicians was Baerauble.  This human wizard was said to be of the blood of the ancient Netherese, who served Ondeth Obarskyr as advisor and his son Faerlthann as Royal Wizard and ambassador.  An elf-friend, Baerauble and his heirs have served the realm as advisors and court wizards for over a millennia. 

Baerauble's heirs were of mixed human-elf blood and most of them long outlived the Obarskyr kings they served.  It is generally acknowledged that the long lifespans of the Royal Magicians of Cormyr have greatly contributed to the stability and wise rule of the realm over the centuries, though at the cost of perpetuating a persistent conservative leaning within the Royal Court.

While the conservative nature of the Royal Court in Suzail looks down upon the Sembian merchants as lesser beings in the social hierarchy of the realm, there is no denying that the wealth of Sembia is far greater than that of Cormyr and that Sembian gold buys great influence and power. 

There is also no denying that the fortunes of the noble houses of Cormyr have changed much over the years as Sembian gold aids first one house and then another.

There have been many threats to the Kingdom of Cormyr over the centuries, but no peril has ever been as great as that faced by King Galaghard III and High Wizard Thanderahast in the Year of the Thirsty Sword. 

In that year a great host of goblins, orcs, ogres, and human mercenaries had allied itself with a vast army of undead under the control of a powerful Order of Necromancers from the East, known as the Witch Lords. The Witch Lords' purpose was plain - they meant to conquer and enslave Cormyr.  Master tacticians as well as fell sorcerers, the Witch Lords' lieutenants flew on great shrieking bats, while the most powerful of the great necromancers commanded the battlefield astride large wyverns of the deep forest. Armored in fear as well as steel, the Witch Lords were said to inspire dread in any mortal who gazed upon them.
 
Despite the whole of the marshalled knights of the kingdom and the disciplined Purple Dragons, Cormyr nearly fell to the Witch Lords in a great battle between what was then the border between the Hullack Forest and the Vast Swamp.  But as the necromancers' army was set to sweep aside the left flank of the defenders and encircle the King's remaining knights, an elven army emerged out of the woods and onto the battlefield.

Taking the Witch Lords by surprise, the army of the elves shattered the orc lines. At a stroke, the mortal soldiers of the Witch Lords were broken and fled the field. With grim determination, the remaining undead host of the Witch Lords was put to the sword by the combined might of Cormyr and the elven King, Othorion Keove.  And so it was that the Kingdom of Cormyr was preserved.

"To whomever it may concern:

I have few wishes for me after my death: my belongings are to be split between my children. My old magic blade, now broken, I would also like kept by one of them and reforged if it is possible to do so.

My only wish for myself after my death is to be buried in the old family graveyard, which can be found in the town of Thunderstone in Cormyr. After my death I would like to return there, and maybe my old bones will watch over Sir Hawklin, who was a good master in life.

My children, if this Will rests in your hands, and I have fallen in battle, please, claim whatever remains of me for burial. I wish you well in your lives. May you continue to make me proud."

The Wyvern Crown of Cormyr is fashioned from pure star metal hewn from the heart of a meteor which crashed into the Wyvernwater long ago. The Crown is studded with numerous jewels, including beljurils, black sapphires, emeralds, and rubies. Set in the center of the Crown is a flawless diamond the size of a human male's fist. When struck by a bright light, the Crown scintillates and sends forth reflective rays in all directions from its gem-tipped spikes.
